title: PHB 85 (NSIC Rc 664H) Hybrid Rice: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaTitle: PHB 85 (NSIC Rc 664H): Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaDescription: PHB 85 is NSIC Rc 664H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland approved in 2021. See its pest ratings, grain quality and where it grows best.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 664H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as PHB 85 and known locally as Mestiso 116. The NSIC approved it in 2021. Corteva bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, but its pest ratings and grain quality are below.

heroImage.alt: Ripe palay heads, the harvest a hybrid like NSIC Rc 664H is bred to fill

blocks.text: If you came here looking for PHB 85, or rice variety 664H, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

blocks.text: How many days does it take, and how much does it yield?

PhilRice has not published this variety's days to harvest and trial yields in its catalogue yet. So ask the seed seller or your municipal agriculturist for the figures from the trials in your region before you plan the season. Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it. Meanwhile, our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare) covers the habits that matter with any variety.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is PHB 85 the same as NSIC Rc 664H?
items.a: Yes. PHB 85 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 664H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 116. The numbers on this page are PhilRice's for NSIC Rc 664H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 664H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 116. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.
The NSIC approved it in 2021. Corteva bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, so ask for the regional trial figures before you plant.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has intermediate amylose, 20.7 percent. So it cooks soft but not sticky.
